lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: proving angle properties of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle
lessonRef.title: Targeted correction: proving angle properties of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Each example contains the correction, not just the answer.

items.prompt: An inscribed angle intercepts a 100° arc. Find it.

steps: Inscribed angle is half the arc.

items.prompt: Radius 3, external point 5 from centre. Tangent length?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Before solving, say which error the problem is testing for.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 4. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 90°, in terms of π.
A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 62°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.
An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 96°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
A circle has radius 5. From an external point 13 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 18, because the tangent extends beyond the circle
12, because the tangent bisects the radius
8, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
12, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 3. Find the arc length and the sector area for a central angle of 120°, in terms of π.
A quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle. One angle measures 111°. Find the measure of the opposite angle.
An inscribed angle in a circle intercepts an arc of 168°. Find the measure of the inscribed angle.
A circle has radius 3. From an external point 5 from the centre, a tangent is drawn. Find the length of the tangent segment, and state the fact that makes this possible.
choices: 8, because the tangent extends beyond the circle
4, because the tangent bisects the radius
4, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
2, because the radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of tangency
